### 2026-10-11 – Managed to make do on a plane with an iPad and managed to code the front-end dash for the project. While I haven’t tested it, the code works in VSCode and it would bug out anyway due to the fact that

**2h**

Managed to make do on a plane with an iPad and managed to code the front-end dash for the project. While I haven’t tested it, the code works in VSCode and it would bug out anyway due to the fact that I have no data to feed it.
The next step is to code the backend in both Python and JS to link the sensor data to the main dash. While I will be on a massive time crunch, I’m fairly sure that I can get the 10hrs done and then I’ll make up some hours to get the best printer over the next few weeks.

### 2026-10-11 – Managed to finish up the project in time. Managed to borrow a laptop and did the whole of the javascript code done that will now update the website based of the JSON dump from the Python code. The pyt

**4.5h**

Managed to finish up the project in time. Managed to borrow a laptop and did the whole of the javascript code done that will now update the website based of the JSON dump from the Python code. The python code is basic but it's rigorous in it's testing and is made to help me when building the real hardware later on. It first initializes the sensors while testing them. Then, it gets the readings from the sensors every second and then dumps it alongside elapsed time.

Also had to get AI to come in and help me adapt a micropython driver for the BMI270 into a circuitpython ready one. I hope that the custom driver will work but we will have to wait and see.

The website has a brand new look after I talked with friends who all know coding better than me. The website holds basic example data that will get updated once I build the project. I also managed to fix all my formatting errors from coding on word!
